title: Choose the visual world for ramondeleonca
question: A fresh hand: three new directions with first-screen sketches. Keep Rótulo, take another, or re-roll again.

options.label: Rótulo
options.lineage: Mexican hand-painted shop signs and painted walls
options.thesis: The site is a painted shopfront wall that announces, line by line, what Ramón makes.
materials: block lettering with a painted shade
one shop window for photos and video
options.viewport: A mango-yellow wall with the name in red block letters, three painted service lines, a black-framed window playing match video, and a cobalt band along the foot carrying the navigation.
options.risk: Charming to clients, but a recruiter may read it as a joke, and it only works if the lettering is drawn well.

raised.raise: A locked paint set: five paints and nothing in between, with shades made from a second flat colour and never a gradient.
Reading text always sits on plain wall, never across lettering or pattern.
Each section gets one large painted figure, with the smaller pieces arranged around it.
Lettering sizes step on one fixed scale, the way a sign painter's brushes do.
A selected line is repainted in a second colour, a visible change of paint instead of a glow or underline.

options.label: Wiring Diagram
options.thesis: Ramón drawn as one control system: robots on the yellow and green bus, websites on the blue line.
options.viewport: Name and one sentence at the top; below, a controller block wired to each project in date order, with education as the power supply and contact as the radio.
options.risk: Boxes joined by lines are a familiar tech picture, and web clients will not know the wire colours.

options.label: Vitral
options.lineage: steel-framed glass wall with a few coloured panes
options.thesis: The whole portfolio as one glass wall: clear panes show the work, coloured panes say what matters.
options.viewport: A wall of panes in black bars: a tall cobalt pane with the name, a clear pane with a robot photo, an amber pane for MechaLeague, and an oxblood pane for contact.
options.case: Clearer than the painted wall, since everything is visible in one elevation; loses on recognition, since it belongs to neither audience's world.
options.risk: Built loosely it is a grid of boxes with thick borders, and the clear panes need good photos.

options.label: Candy Poster
options.thesis: Each section as an illustrated poster in flat candy colour.
options.viewport: One black robot silhouette blooming into coloured ribbons, with the name hand-lettered above.
options.case: The painted wall already gives the lettered-poster feeling with a Mexican root; this one is American and needs illustration that does not exist yet.
options.kept: One anchoring image per section with smaller pieces around it.

options.label: Sixteen Colours
options.thesis: A fixed pixel screen with a text window below and a portrait at the right.
materials: bitmap type on a cell grid
options.viewport: A dithered scene with a bordered text window listing projects along the bottom.
options.case: Retro-game nostalgia is not his world, and bitmap type slows a one-minute read.
options.kept: A locked colour set with no in-between tones.
options.risk: Reads as a game, not a portfolio.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Glowing orange digits in glass tubes count the work.
options.viewport: Banks of glowing digits for years, teams and awards on a dark panel.
options.case: A dark page with one glowing accent and big numbers is the look the old attempt was already heading toward.
options.kept: State changes shown as visible physical events.
options.risk: Numbers stand in for the work itself.

options.label: Cloud Edge
options.thesis: A white page with a thin pastel fringe marking what is active.
options.viewport: Wide white margins, quiet text, and a mint-to-violet edge on the current section.
options.case: Calm and readable, but nothing in it says robots, Saltillo or building things.
options.kept: Body text stays on a plain, colourless field.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Translucent sheets with hatching stacked over a grey step ramp.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets, each holding one project, hatched by how much weight it carries.
options.case: Made for dense working screens, and darkroom printing is foreign to both audiences.
options.kept: One fixed tonal and size ramp for all hierarchy.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean developer portfolio everyone recognises, built carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Name, one-line role and two buttons, then a grid of project cards, about, and contact.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other portfolios by design.
